title: What to put in a freelance retainer agreement (and a template)
summary: What is a retainer agreement and what should it include? Learn the key clauses for freelancers and grab a free template to adapt. Get started now.
body_markdown:
Imagine finishing a successful project for a client, only to find yourself negotiating another contract a few weeks later. You're back to discussing rates, agreeing on deadlines, and figuring out when the next payment will arrive. Now, imagine having that same client pay you consistently every month for ongoing work. That's where a retainer agreement comes in.


A **retainer agreement** is a contract where a client pays a freelancer a fixed fee on a recurring basis in exchange for ongoing services or availability. It outlines the scope of work, fees, payment terms, agreed hours or deliverables, and how either party can end the arrangement.


For example, a freelance graphic designer might receive a monthly fee to create social media graphics, design promotional materials, and handle regular brand updates. The agreement establishes the expected deliverables, deadlines, and additional charges for requests outside the original scope.


It should also address revisions, unused hours, late payments, and termination notice. These details protect your time, manage client expectations, and ensure both parties understand their responsibilities. With clear terms in place, you can spend less time chasing new projects and more time building stable, long-term client relationships.


## **What is a retainer agreement?**


A retainer agreement is a contract where a client pays a freelancer a fixed fee on a recurring basis for ongoing services or availability. It outlines the scope of work, payment terms, deliverables, timelines and responsibilities of both parties. For example, a freelance writer might receive $800 monthly to produce eight articles and provide editorial support.


Retainer agreements are particularly useful when clients need your services regularly rather than for one-off projects. However, before settling on this arrangement, consider how you operate as a freelancer. Understanding[whether you need an LLC as a freelancer](https://grey.co/blog/llc-vs-sole-proprietorship) and the differences between a[contractor vs. employee](http://grey.co/blog/contractor-vs-employee) can help you clarify your business structure, responsibilities, and working relationship with clients. These considerations also make it easier to establish retainer terms that suit your business and the services you provide.


Here are four benefits of a retainer agreement:


- **Predictable income:** Being certain that a client will pay you $1200 every month makes it easier to budget, save and manage business expenses.
- **Stronger client relationships:** Working continuously with a client helps you understand their business, audience and expectations.
- **Better workload planning:** Agreed deliverables and hours help you manage capacity and avoid overcommitting.
- **Less time finding clients:** Recurring engagements reduce the pressure to constantly pitch for new projects to maintain your income.


## **Types of retainer agreements**


Retainers generally fall into two categories: pay-for-work and pay-for-access, depending on what clients are paying you to provide.


If you're comparing retainers with other ways of charging clients, Grey's[freelance pricing models](https://grey.co/blog/freelance-pricing-models) explains how hourly, project-based and retainer arrangements differ.


### **1. Pay-for-work retainer**


With a pay-for-work retainer, a client pays you a recurring fee for an agreed amount of work or specific deliverables. You know what you are expected to produce, and the client knows what they are paying for. For example, a freelance social media manager might charge $1,000 monthly to manage three platforms, create 20 posts and provide monthly performance reports. Any work outside the agreed scope attracts an additional fee.


### **2. Pay-for-access retainer**


A pay-for-access retainer means a client pays to secure your availability and expertise when needed, rather than for a fixed number of deliverables. Lawyers commonly use this arrangement, charging clients a recurring fee to retain their services and access legal advice when issues arise. Similarly, a freelance consultant might charge $500 monthly to be available for strategy calls, urgent consultations and professional advice, even when the client does not need support every week.


## **What to include in your freelance retainer agreement**


Before signing, make sure your retainer agreement covers these seven areas. Each one helps establish clear expectations, protect your time and prevent disagreements as the working relationship develops.


### **1. Scope of work**


Define the services you will provide and the deliverables expected within each billing cycle. A freelance graphic designer may agree to create 12 social media graphics and two promotional banners each month. You can use a[statement of work (SOW)](https://grey.co/blog/statement-of-work) to document these deliverables, timelines, and responsibilities, including what falls outside the agreed scope and attracts additional fees.


### **2. Retainer fee**


State the agreed fee, currency and billing frequency. Whether you charge $500 or $2,000 monthly, ensure the amount reflects your workload, expertise and the value you provide. Also clarify whether the fee is fixed or subject to review after an agreed period.


### **3. Payment terms**


Specify when invoices are issued, payment deadlines and accepted payment methods. For example, you might require clients to pay on the first of every month before work begins. Include provisions for late payments, missed payments and any applicable penalties.


### **4. Hours and availability**


Clarify the working hours covered by the retainer, your availability and expected response times. If your agreement includes 15 hours per month, explain how additional hours will be billed and whether unused hours roll over to the next billing cycle.


### **5. Revisions**


Establish how many revision rounds are included and what qualifies as additional work. For instance, you might offer two rounds of revisions per article. Requests that require a complete rewrite or change the original brief should attract additional fees.


### **6. Intellectual property**


Explain who owns the completed work and when ownership transfers. You might agree that clients receive full ownership of approved deliverables upon payment, while you retain the right to showcase selected projects in your portfolio, subject to confidentiality agreements.


### **7. Termination**


State how either party can end the agreement, including notice periods and outstanding payment obligations. For example, you could require 30 days' written notice before termination. Also clarify how unfinished assignments, final invoices and access to completed work will be handled.


## **Free freelance retainer agreement template**


Use this simplified template to outline your working arrangement with a client. Fill in the relevant details, agree on the terms and have both parties sign before work begins.


**Effective date:**


**Client:** Client Name


**Freelancer:** Your Name / Business Name


**1. Scope of services**


The Freelancer agrees to provide the following services:


- \[List agreed services and deliverables\]
- \[Specify monthly hours or availability\]


Any work outside this scope will require separate approval and additional fees.


### **2. Retainer fee and payment**


- **Fee:**
- **Payment date:**
- **Payment deadline:**
- **Additional work:**


### **3. Duration and termination**


This agreement begins on \[Start Date\] and continues on a \[monthly / fixed-term\] basis.


Either party may end the agreement by providing \[30 days\] written notice. Immediate termination may apply if either party breaches the agreement and fails to resolve the issue within \[7 days\] of written notice.


### **4. Independent contractor status**


The Freelancer operates as an independent contractor, not an employee of the Client, and is responsible for their own taxes, insurance and business obligations.


### **5. Confidentiality and ownership**


Both parties agree to protect confidential business information. Ownership of final deliverables transfers to the Client once all outstanding payments have been made, unless otherwise agreed in writing.


### **6. Liability and disputes**


Each party is responsible for claims arising from its own negligence or misconduct. The Freelancer's total liability will not exceed \[agreed amount or fees paid in the preceding three months\], subject to applicable law.


Any disagreement will first be addressed through good-faith discussions, followed by mediation or arbitration if necessary.


### **7. Governing law**


This agreement is governed by the laws of \[State / Country\].


### **8. Signatures**


By signing below, both parties confirm that they understand and accept these terms.

## **Frequently asked questions about freelance retainer agreements**


### **1. What is a retainer agreement?**


A retainer agreement is a contract between a freelancer and a client for ongoing services or availability in exchange for a recurring fee. It outlines the work involved, payment arrangements, timelines and responsibilities, giving both parties clarity and helping freelancers secure more predictable income.


### **2. How does a freelance retainer work?**


A freelance retainer works by establishing a recurring payment for agreed services. You and your client decide on the fee, deliverables, working hours and billing cycle. You then provide the agreed services throughout that period, invoice according to your arrangement and receive payment at the agreed time.


### **3. What should a retainer agreement include?**


A retainer agreement should include the scope of work, recurring fee, payment deadlines, working hours, deliverables, revision limits, intellectual property rights and termination conditions. You should also clarify how additional work, unused hours, confidentiality and expenses will be handled to prevent misunderstandings during the engagement.


### **4. Are retainers paid upfront?**


Yes, many retainers are paid upfront at the beginning of each billing cycle, usually monthly. This allows freelancers to secure payment before committing their time and availability. However, payment arrangements depend on what both parties agree to, so specify invoice dates and deadlines in your contract.


### **5. Can I end a retainer agreement?**


Yes. Most retainer agreements include termination clauses that allow either party to end the arrangement with written notice, typically 14 or 30 days. Check your contract for notice requirements, outstanding payments and unfinished deliverables before ending the engagement to avoid disputes with your client.


### **6. How do I get paid on a retainer from overseas?**


You can receive overseas retainer payments through international bank transfers or multi-currency payment platforms. With Grey, you can open a USD, GBP or EUR account to receive client payments, hold foreign currency and transfer your earnings to your local Nigerian bank account when needed.
